newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU centrist leaders see EMU on track.
newsitem.headline: EU centrist leaders see EMU on track.

text.p: European Union (EU) centrist leaders insisted on Tuesday that economic and monetary union (EMU) was still on track and that delaying the single currency was highly undesirable.
"It is very important to stick to the timetable," Irish Prime Minister John Bruton told reporters as he arrived for a summit of the European People's Party, a mainly Christian Democrat grouping.
"There is a clear determination on behalf of member states," he said.

The centrists, including German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar and Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi, were due to discuss a number of key issues facing the 15-nation bloc.
Formally, the agenda called for discussions about the state of the inter-governmental conference (IGC), the EU's treaty reform and the bloc's planned enlargement into eastern Europe.

But officials said it would be next to impossible for the leaders not to discuss EMU, particularly given market rumours of a possible delay and the struggle of a number of countries, including Germany, to meet EMU standards.
Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker warned against putting back the January 1, 1999 start for the single currency.
"It is not a good idea to delay EMU," he said, noting that the old European Community once delayed a plan for a defence union and that it has never achieved it since.
Juncker also repeated the litany of EU leaders that all countries that qualify for the single currency will join EMU, regardless of their geography.
"There is no thought of excluding the southern members states," Juncker said. "There is no Club Med."
He was using EU jargon for the southern EU members of Spain, Portugal, Italy and Greece whose economies are considered the weakest in the bloc.
